title: Asian Stir Fry Vegetables, Cooked, Fat Added

content.title: About
content.content: Asian stir‑fry vegetables are a blend of sliced vegetables (broccoli, carrots, bell peppers, snap peas, mushrooms, etc.) that have been lightly sautéed in a small amount of oil. The product is ready to eat – simply reheat in a wok or microwave.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The mix often includes vegetables typical for Asian cuisine such as bamboo shoots and water chestnuts.
Vegetables cook quickly – usually 3‑5 minutes over high heat.
Adding a modest amount of fat enhances flavor and aids absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.
The product is commonly used in wok and street‑food dishes in fast‑casual restaurants.
Formulations are often gluten‑free and contain no added sugar.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: The vegetables provide vitamin B6 and folate, which support metabolism and nervous‑system function.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Broccoli and bell peppers are high in vitamin C and carotenoids that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber promotes healthy bowel movements and contributes to satiety.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: When the added oil is kept moderate, a serving contains few calories, making it suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Improves nutrient absorption
items.content: A small amount of fat helps the body better absorb fat‑soluble vitamins A, D, E, and K.

items.title: Allergy to specific vegetables
items.content: Some individuals may react to soy sauce, sesame, or other ingredients sometimes included in the blend.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Certain versions may contain added soy sauce, increasing the salt level.

items.title: Excess fat intake
items.content: Using too much added oil can raise the calorie count and strain the digestive system.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the vegetables over high heat for 3‑5 minutes, optionally adding soy sauce, ginger, or garlic. Serve as a side dish, over rice or noodles, or as the main component of a wok‑style stir‑fry.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 0‑4 °C in the original packaging or an airtight container for up to 5 days. After opening, use within 2‑3 days for best quality.
